svg.title: Localized AI: crawler files, locale-aware retrieval and LoRA adapters chosen by consent
svg.desc: Two channels that never mix. The content channel: public pages pass robots.txt and llms.txt, which are public requests rather than access control, to crawlers: Googlebot for Search and AI Overviews, Google-Extended for Gemini, Storebot-Google for Merchant Center, and AI tools that read llms.txt. The consent channel: the Shopify Customer Privacy API gives the consent state, the edge attaches it to every event, and Google receives Consent Mode v2 states and Customer Match consent fields, while the Merchant API carries products only. Allowing a crawler is never consent to use a person's data. Localized retrieval loads each locale, tags every chunk with locale, market, canonical ID and translation source, embeds all locales in one multilingual index, retrieves the user's locale first with an English fallback, and answers in the user's language with live prices. LoRA adapters: a request's locale, market and consent go to an adapter picker; no consent gives the language adapter with public chunks, preferences add stated preferences, preferences and marketing unlock a personalization adapter with a cohort label. Personalization adapters are trained only on records consented for training, inside the clean room, registered with a dataset hash, and retired and retrained without people who withdrew. Rules for the EU and UK, the US, South Korea and Japan, and ten red gaps with fixes.
svg.text: LOCALIZED AI — CRAWLER FILES vs CONSENT, LOCALE-AWARE RETRIEVAL, LoRA CHOSEN BY CONSENT
crawler files decide which content AI may read; consent decides which people your systems may use
A · Content channel — which content AI may read
B · Consent channel — which people your systems may use
Customer names or orders in JSON-LD
Crawl permission read as consent: it never is
LOCALIZED RETRIEVAL — FILTER BY LOCALE FIRST, THEN FALL BACK
the user's locale and market first;
fetch the price live, not embedded
Stale price from the vector store
Locale guessed from the IP address
LoRA ADAPTERS — THE LOCALE PICKS THE LANGUAGE, CONSENT UNLOCKS PERSONALIZATION
No consent, or denied: language adapter
the query and public retrieved chunks only
plus stated preferences such as size or language; no history
plus a cohort label and recent views; never raw personal data
the ledger records the adapter, locale,
market and consent state of every answer
Withdrawn consent stays in the weights
Personalization served without a consent check
Global Privacy Control. Train only on
Separate consent for use beyond the
Language adapter only until in-country storage.
TEN GAPS — AND THE FIX FOR EACH
Fix: Protect sensitive paths with authentication; a Disallow line publishes the path
Fix: Generate it from an allowlist of public URLs, never from the whole CMS
Fix: Separate channels; check the consent state on every event
Fix: No customer names or order details in JSON-LD: it is published with no consent check
Stale price from the vector store
Fix: Never answer price or availability from embeddings; fetch live by country
Fix: Only human-translated chunks for legal and claims text
Locale guessed from the IP address
Fix: Explicit choice, then market, then Accept-Language; apply that locale's rules
Fix: A separate training scope per record; dataset_hash and record_count in the ledger
Withdrawn consent stays in the weights
Fix: Scheduled retirement (retire_by) and a retrain without the withdrawn
Fix: Check consent and blocked markets on every request; fall back to the language adapter
Crawler files decide which content AI reads. Consent decides which people your systems use. The ledger records which adapter answered, under which consent.
